newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Gas oil slumps on prompt surplus.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Gas oil slumps on prompt surplus.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices fell sharply late Monday as desperate sellers cut their prices drastically in the face of high stocks in an effort to resolve ullage problems, traders said.
The sharp drop in gas oil prices has led to an improvement in the jet fuel/gas oil spread as the jet market is not as over supplied as the gas oil market, they said.
Gas oil prices fell by almost $1.00 per barrel over Friday as sellers came out in force to ensure a sale in the wake of poor regional enduser demand.
A 150,000 barrel cargo traded late day at $22.20 per barrel free-on-board Singapore for July 1-5 lifting, down from Friday's $22.95 lowest offered level.
The deal was between a U.S. major and an European major.
Early last week, one cargo traded at $22.80 per barrel, down $1.40 from the previous traded level.
"The physical overhang is starting to take its toll. People think this market is going to be thrashed," one trader said, signalling further price cuts.
Traders said the market will only rebound if a new round of large purchases emerge from either large regional endsuers or traders purchasing from the local spot market.
At the moment stocks remain high and sellers are lost seeking fresh outlets for their output.
As a result, one refiner, Shell Singapore has already announced a near seven percent cut in output at its 430,000 barrel per day refinery.
The cut is expected to have minimal impact due to the high stocks but it will at least send message that refiners are trying to resolve the problem, traders said.
Latest data from the Trade Development Board showed middle distillate stocks in the week ending June 11 rose 993,000 barrels to 11.236 million barrels, the highest since at least January 1994.
The rising middle distillate stock level in Singapore has already forced some refiners to store product outside their refinery system on a spot basis.
Last week, one refiner sold a prompt spot 30,000-tonne cargo at a 40-cent discount to spot Singapore quotes on a free-on-board basis due to tight ullage, compared to the prevailing 10 cents discount.
The weak market was also seen in the swaps market where July gas oil was last quoted at $22.50/$22.60 per barrel, down sharply from Friday's $23.15/$23.25, brokers said.
As a result of the plunge in gas oil prices, the jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) widened as outright jet fuel prices were fairly steady.
July regrade was last quoted at 50/80 cents from Friday's 30/40 cents, brokers said.
Physical jet fuel was offered down to a low of $23.60 per barrel, compared to the $22.20 per barrel gas oil trade.
